title: Staged Variance Heatmap — Wires and Grooming
content:
Context / Why this doc

This is a working design + grooming artifact for a variant of the rollouts UI focused on surfacing per-metric variance across staged traffic shifts. Goal: give operators a fast, simulation-first view to (1) preview how small traffic increments change metric variance (p95 latency, quality regression score, token cost), (2) make it easy to set automated fallback thresholds, and (3) reduce manual trial-and-error when running canary / phased A/B experiments.

What problem we observed
- Operators run canaries but only get coarse aggregated metrics (avg latency, success rate) which hide distribution changes.
- When a rollback trigger is configured by a single metric threshold, teams either overfit (too sensitive) or under-react (too lax).
- Current console requires separate experiments to test fallback thresholds — long feedback loop.

High-level proposal
- Add a "Staged Variance" panel into the rollouts composer. This panel contains a heatmap (traffic % vs metric variance), a decision simulator, and a quick-config for automated fallback policies.
- The heatmap visualizes per-interval variance (std dev or IQR) for selected KPIs across traffic slices (0% -> 100%). Each row is a KPI, each column a discrete traffic bucket (0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100). Colors indicate change from baseline (green = improvement, red = degradation, amber = high variance).
- Decision simulator: operator defines a hypothetical staged rollout (e.g., 0->5->25->50 over 24h) and the simulator projects the probability of triggering the fallback using historical distributions and current sample sizes.

Prototype wireframes (notes for engineering / design)
- Layout: left column = preview panel (compact traffic slider + quick metrics snapshot). Center = heatmap (expandable). Right = simulator + fallback configuration + microcopy help.
- Heatmap interactions: hover shows tooltip with exact metric delta, sample size, and confidence interval. Click a cell to open a small temporal chart of metric over historical windows for that traffic bucket.
- Simulator controls: choose traffic steps, dwell time per step, confidence threshold (95/90), and whether to use one-sided or two-sided tests. "Run simulation" returns a % chance of hitting fallback at each stage and a timeline with expected SLO-impact bands.
- Fallback wiring: quick toggles for "Immediate rollback" vs "Gradual step-down" (e.g., step down by 50% then re-evaluate). Add option to "Notify and wait" which pauses automatic rollback and notifies the operator.

Microcopy and inline help (suggestions)
- Heatmap title: "Expected variance vs traffic — predicts how metrics change as traffic shifts to the new variant."
- Simulator brief: "Simulate staged rollouts using historical variance to estimate fallback risk. Useful when sample sizes are small."
- Fallback tooltip: "If the configured condition is met at any stage, the selected fallback action will execute. Use conservative thresholds for low-traffic canaries."

Operator flows (user stories)
1) Quick safety check (SRE): ``As an SRE, I want to preview whether a 5% canary will materially increase p95 latency so I can decide whether to proceed.`` -> open rollout composer -> select variant -> open Staged Variance panel -> view heatmap row for p95 -> hover on 5% cell -> decide to increase preflight tests.
2) Configure automated fallback (product infra): ``As a platform engineer, I want to set a fallback that kicks in if quality score degrades by >5% with 95% confidence during any stage, but otherwise let the rollout continue." -> use simulator to test thresholds -> set autofallback with "notify and wait" for first two stages.
3) Post-mortem simulation (PM): "Re-run simulated rollout of the incident to understand if different dwell times would have avoided a bad rollback."

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Heatmap shows at least 4 KPIs (p50 latency, p95 latency, quality-regression-score, cost-per-1000-tokens) across predefined traffic buckets.
- Tooltips include delta, baseline, sample size, and 95% CI.
- Simulator can accept a staged plan (up to 6 steps) and returns per-stage fallback probability.
- UI allows binding the simulated threshold to an actual rollback policy when operator clicks "Promote to policy".
- Feature gated behind an org-level flag and visible only to org admins / operators in beta.

Backlog (rough order + rough estimates)
- PROD-2410 (3d): Data: aggregation endpoint for variance by traffic bucket (histogram bins) + sample sizes.
- PROD-2467 (5d): Frontend: heatmap component with tooltip + cell drilldown chart.
- PROD-2479 (4d): Simulation engine: simple Monte Carlo using historical variance or bootstrap resampling.
- PROD-2483 (2d): UX: microcopy + help panel + tour.
- PROD-2491 (2d): Policy binding: create rollback policy from simulation output.
- PROD-2500 (1d): Feature flag + permission checks.
- Nice-to-have (future): link to live traces for cells that exceed threshold; historical compare mode across model versions.

Edge cases and open questions
- Low-sample buckets: how to present heatmap cells when sample size < N_min? (proposed: hatch pattern + tooltip "not enough data").
- Correlated regressions: simulator assumes independent metrics; for correlated regressions (latency + quality) we may need multivariate sampling. Is that necessary for MVP? (conclusion: no, model later).
- Rolling windows vs fixed windows: which historical window to use? Default = last 14 days, but allow override.
- Legal / privacy: ensure simulation uses aggregated metrics only, no raw request payloads.

UI copy examples (for devs to implement)
- Button: "Run rollout simulation"
- Secondary: "Promote thresholds to rollback policy"
- Inline label: "Traffic buckets (preview): 0,1,5,10,25,50,75,100"
- Warning when promote: "This will create an automatic fallback that triggers when configured conditions are met. Review sample sizes before enabling auto rollback."

Design notes for accessibility
- Heatmap should be colorblind-friendly palette + textual legend. Include pattern overlays for extreme cases.
- All interactive cells keyboard-focusable and accessible via aria-label including metric name, bucket, delta.

Telemetry/Observability hooks (implementation notes)
- Record simulator usage events (simulate.started, simulate.completed, simulate.promoted_to_policy).
- Tag metrics with rollout_id, org_id, user_id for audit.
- Emit an explanation payload when a promoted policy triggers a rollback (which simulator scenario predicted it).

Prototype links and references
- Early lo-fi sketches in Figma: link placeholder -> /figma/staged-variance (internal)
- Related design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Variance+Heatmap+Design+Notes
- Engineering tickets above (PROD-2410, PROD-2467, PROD-2479)

Next steps (today / this sprint)
- Align with Data for variance-by-traffic endpoint (owner: Marcus).
- Designer to produce hi-fi heatmap states and accessible color palette (owner: Aisha).
- Devs to spike Monte Carlo simulator approach vs bootstrap and report perf/latency (owner: Tomás).
- Add tickets to backlog, link to this doc, and schedule a 30m sync to lock on MVP scope.

Notes to reviewers
- Focus feedback on: is the heatmap the right view (vs small multiples)? Are the proposed traffic buckets too coarse? Are the simulator assumptions reasonable?
- Please add comments inline or drop thoughts in #rollouts-product on Slack.

-- end --
